name: COMSOL Multiphysics
version_reference: 6.4 (verified against a local installation: help, completion data, plugins and Application Library)
description: COMSOL Multiphysics is a finite-element simulation platform for coupled physics problems. Work is organised in the Model Builder tree: Global Definitions holds parameters, variables and functions; each Component carries its own Definitions, Geometry, Materials, one or more physics interfaces, and a Mesh; Studies define what to solve (stationary, time dependent, frequency domain, eigenfrequency, parametric sweeps) and own the Solver Configurations; Results holds datasets, derived values, plot groups, exports and reports. Physics interfaces supply the governing equations and boundary conditions for structural mechanics, heat transfer, fluid flow, acoustics, electromagnetics, chemical species transport, electrochemistry, semiconductors, plasma, particle tracing and general PDEs, and Multiphysics coupling nodes join them (thermal expansion, Joule heating, fluid-structure interaction, piezoelectricity). Everything in the tree maps one-to-one onto the COMSOL API for Java, so any model can be recorded as a .java or .m file, edited, and replayed headless. The Application Builder adds a Form Editor and a Java Method Editor for turning models into apps that run in COMSOL Server or are compiled to standalone executables with COMSOL Compiler.

automation.summary: COMSOL is scripted through one object model exposed in several languages. (1) Headless batch: `comsol batch -inputfile m.mph -outputfile out.mph` (or the `comsolbatch` shortcut) solves a saved model with no GUI, optionally overriding parameters (`-pname`/`-plist`), choosing a study (`-study`) and setting process/node counts (`-np`, `-nn`). `comsol batch -inputfile job.java` compiles and runs a Java model file; `comsol compile` and `comsol server` cover compilation and client/server use. (2) COMSOL API for Java: the canonical form of the tree, with `ModelUtil.create`, `model.param()`, `model.component()`, `model.geom()`, `model.physics()`, `model.mesh()`, `model.study()`, `model.sol()` and `model.result()`. Any GUI session can emit exactly this code with File > Save As .java or Compact History. (3) LiveLink for MATLAB: the same Java objects wrapped for MATLAB, plus `mph*` convenience functions (`mphstart`, `mphload`, `mphsolve`, `mpheval`, `mphint2`, `mphglobal`, `mphplot`, `mphnavigator`). (4) MPh, a community Python package layered on JPype that drives the same Java API (`mph.start()`, `client.load()`, `model.solve()`, `model.evaluate()`, `model.export()`). (5) Model Methods and Application Builder methods run Java inside the running COMSOL session and can be called from batch with `-methodcall`. In all cases the workflow is identical: set parameters, build geometry, assign materials and physics, build mesh, run study, evaluate results, export.

cli.description: Solve a saved model headless and write the solved model to a new file. If `-outputfile` is omitted the solution is written back into the input file. This is the standard non-interactive entry point; on Windows the `comsolbatch.exe` shortcut does the same thing without opening a console window.
Run one named study only and capture the solver log to a text file. Study tags (`std1`, `std2`, ...) are visible in the Model Builder property window or with `model.study().tags()`.

Override global parameters on the command line before solving. `-pname` takes a comma-separated list of parameter names and `-plist` the matching values with units; use `-paramfile` to read many parameter sets from a file instead.
Run shared-memory parallel on 8 cores. `-nn` sets the number of distributed (MPI) nodes for cluster runs, `-nnhost` the nodes per host, and `-f hostfile` supplies the host list.

Compile and execute a COMSOL API Java model file in one step, so a model can be generated entirely from source without ever opening the GUI. Use `comsol compile buildmodel.java` to produce a `.class` file separately.

Run a Model Method (Application Builder / Method Editor Java code stored in the model) in batch. Combine with `-recover` to continue from the last stored solution after a crash and `-continue` to resume an interrupted parametric run.

Start a COMSOL Multiphysics Server that LiveLink clients (MATLAB, Python/MPh, Java) connect to. `comsol mphserver matlab` starts the server and a MATLAB session already connected to it; `comsol server/client` runs the full GUI against a remote server.
Compile a COMSOL API Java file into a `.class` file, or compile an application (`.mphapp`) into a standalone executable with COMSOL Compiler. Requires the bundled JDK path when `-jdk` is used.

apis.name: COMSOL API for Java
apis.description: The native scripting interface and the reference form of every other binding. A `Model` object mirrors the Model Builder tree exactly: each node is created with `.create(tag, type)`, configured with `.set(property, value)` and selected with `.selection().set(...)`. The fastest way to learn it is to build a model in the GUI and save it as Java (File > Save As > Model File for Java), then trim the generated code. Java model files run headless with `comsol batch -inputfile file.java`.

apis.name: LiveLink for MATLAB
apis.description: Exposes the same Java model object inside MATLAB and adds a set of `mph*` helper functions for loading, solving, meshing, evaluating and plotting. Start the connection with `mphstart` (or launch `comsol mphserver matlab`), then use ordinary MATLAB syntax on the model object. Ideal for parameter studies, optimisation loops and post-processing where MATLAB's analysis functions are wanted alongside COMSOL's solvers.

apis.name: MPh (Python)
apis.description: An open-source Python package that talks to the COMSOL Java API through JPype, giving a pythonic wrapper over clients, models, nodes, parameters and solutions. `mph.start()` launches a local COMSOL session (stand-alone or connected to a COMSOL server), `client.load()` opens a `.mph` file, and model methods cover parameters, solving, evaluation, export and saving. The raw Java objects remain reachable through `model.java` for anything the wrapper does not expose.
apis.example:
import mph
client = mph.start(cores=4)
model = client.load('busbar.mph')
model.parameter('Vtot', '20[mV]')
model.solve('Study 1')
print(model.evaluate('2*nojac(comp1.ec.normE)', 'W'))
model.export('Data 1', 'field.txt')
model.save('busbar_out.mph')
client.remove(model)

apis.name: Application Builder and Method Editor
apis.description: The Form Editor builds a custom user interface (inputs, buttons, graphics, tables) on top of a model, and the Method Editor holds Java methods that read and write the model tree, run studies and drive the forms. Model Methods are the same Java code stored in an ordinary `.mph` and callable from the GUI, from other methods or from batch with `-methodcall`. Applications are shared through COMSOL Server or turned into standalone executables with COMSOL Compiler.

apis.name: LiveLink products for CAD and other tools
apis.description: Bidirectional links that keep COMSOL synchronised with external software: LiveLink for SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, AutoCAD, Revit, PTC Creo Parametric, PTC Pro/ENGINEER and Solid Edge associate a parametric CAD assembly with a COMSOL geometry; LiveLink for Excel exposes parameters and results in a spreadsheet; LiveLink for Simulink exports a COMSOL model as an S-function block for control design. The CAD Import Module and ECAD Import Module read neutral and board formats without a live link.

file_formats.description: COMSOL Multiphysics model file: a compressed binary container with the whole Model Builder tree, geometry, mesh, settings, optionally the computed solution and any embedded application forms and methods. The unit of work for `comsol batch`, `mphload` and `client.load`.
Standalone COMSOL application (model plus Application Builder forms and methods) saved for distribution through COMSOL Server or for compilation into an executable with COMSOL Compiler.
Binary COMSOL geometry/mesh interchange file. Written by Geometry > Export and read by the Import node; compact and exact, but only readable by COMSOL.
Text version of .mphbin holding geometry objects or mesh data in a documented ASCII layout. Useful for generating meshes or geometry from an external script.

COMSOL API model file produced by File > Save As > Model File for Java (or Compact History). Human-readable source that rebuilds the whole model; compile with `comsol compile` or run directly with `comsol batch -inputfile`.
Compiled COMSOL API Java model or method, produced by `comsol compile`. Runs headless with `comsol batch -inputfile Model.class` without recompiling.
LiveLink for MATLAB model file written by File > Save As > Model File for MATLAB. Contains the same sequence of API calls in MATLAB syntax and can be edited and re-run like any script.
Model file for use with LiveLink for Excel / VBA automation, generated by File > Save As > Model File for VBA.
Batch status files and the recovery directory COMSOL writes during long runs. `-recover` restarts a batch job from the last stored solution using this data.

Common result export formats from Results > Export > Data: spreadsheet/sectionwise text, comma-separated values and VTK unstructured grid for ParaView. Images export as PNG/JPEG/TIFF and animations as GIF/AVI/WebM.
